title: Fed Chairman Warsh Seeks to Calm Elevated Inflation Concerns
summary: In a high-profile speech, Kevin M. Warsh said the Federal Reserve was chiefly responsible for taming inflation. If price increases did not return to the central bank’s target quickly, “we have work to do,” he said.

title: Investors Expect Higher Rates After Fed Chairman’s Inflation Pledge
summary: Kevin Warsh reiterated the Federal Reserve’s commitment to tackle rising prices, nudging up investor expectations of a rate increase.

title: Smaller Revision Points to More Accurate Jobs Numbers
summary: The 2026 revisions by the Bureau of Labor Statistics represent a downward adjustment of just 0.1 percent of the total work force.

title: Disaster Experts Say Nepal Glacier Collapse Was Difficult to Predict
summary: Given the challenges in forecasting and detecting such calamities, researchers advised banning construction on floodplains and marking out clear evacuation routes.

title: Six Months In, Iran Appears Stronger and U.S. Goals Unclear
summary: Trump’s replacement of a military war with a heightened economic one is not expected to alter Iran’s strategy, while further impoverishing its people.

title: Why Many Iranians Are Losing Hope After Six Months of War
summary: Iranians have become increasingly desperate, as they grapple with an economic crisis made worse by the conflict and grow increasingly skeptical about President Trump’s motives.

title: You Can Photograph This Pretty Irish Castle. You Just Can’t Go In.
summary: Tourists still flock to the picturesque 16th-century Dunguaire Castle on Galway Bay. But in recent years, a dispute over ownership has prevented visitors from entering.

title: Social Media and the Myth of the Big Tobacco Moment
summary: Smoking used to be everywhere, the way Facebook, TikTok, Snap, YouTube and Instagram are now. Society decided to break the habit, but it took a long time.

title: Why Countries Are Pushing Social Media Bans Despite Their Flaws
summary: Proposals for curbing social media use among children have wide support, but critics say they are ineffective.

title: For Once, a New York Jet Is Destined to Win Something

title: With Term Winding Down, Pelosi Tries to Anoint a Successor
summary: Representative Nancy Pelosi, the former House speaker, has been working hard on behalf of Connie Chan, a San Francisco supervisor with a relatively low profile in California.

title: Wyoming Governor Objects to ‘Very Odd’ D.O.J. Election Monitoring
summary: Governor Mark Gordon, a Republican, said he was concerned by the behavior of election observers who visited a polling station in Cheyenne.

title: China Sees Opportunity in America’s Recent A.I. Security Scares
summary: A leading Chinese A.I. start-up released its latest model and made the case that China’s embrace of open software is safer than Silicon Valley’s closed approach.

summary: Landlords are offering renters in rent-controlled apartments tens of thousands of dollars to leave their homes. For many, it’s not enough.

title: What if the A.I. Stock Market Rally Is Just Getting Started?
summary: Edward Yardeni, an upbeat strategist with an excellent track record in assessing the stock market, explains why he thinks the good times will continue for years.

summary: Her latest novel appears to savage a celebrity. But Cusk has, once again, managed to turn herself into the victim.

summary: A small gene-editing study significantly reduced LDL cholesterol levels, and the results have stuck a year later.

summary: How to understand the wide range of sympathy for a mother on trial for murder.

summary: To reach a verdict, jurors must agree on whether Ms. Clancy should be held criminally responsible for killing her three children.

title: Harald V, Norway’s King as Tradition and Modernity Collided, Dies at 89
summary: His 35-year reign opened an ancient monarchy to marriages with so-called commoners and to an incendiary association with Jeffrey Epstein.
